\chapter{\texorpdfstring{Peer sessions}{Peer sessions}}
\label{chap:peer-sessions}

\textbf{Purpose:} How other sessions that build on the engine take it, so no edit here waits on them and no build of theirs reads a tree in motion.

\textbf{Scope:} the RSNA knee session and the CASMI chemistry session, as of 23 September.

Ruled by Doug, 23 September: the chemistry engine does not take precedence over the engine's own work, and a peer uses a git dependency.

\begin{itemize}
\item Peer sessions (the RSNA fork at D:\textbackslash{}kaggle\textbackslash{}rsna\_\allowbreak{}knee\_\allowbreak{}abnormality\textbackslash{}engine, the CASMI chemistry session at D:\textbackslash{}kaggle\textbackslash{}casmi\_\allowbreak{}2026) build the engine from a git dependency pinned at a commit, never from this working tree in place.
\item Engine source edits are never paused or held because a peer is building. A peer that asks for a hold is refused and pointed at a pinned checkout.
\item Peers are told before a record-API shape change lands in a commit, and GPU runs are coordinated by message until tessera (the device-job scheduler) exists.
\item Commits happen only when Doug asks; peers move their pins then.
\end{itemize}
